The application is a peer-to-peer campus errand platform where students can request items to be collected from campus stores or facilities.
A student can act as a requester by creating an errand for another student to fulfill.
A student can act as a courier by viewing available errands and accepting an errand to complete.
Students can use the platform both to request errands and to fulfill errands for other students.
A requester must specify the campus pickup location and the delivery details when creating an errand.
An errand request includes the location from which the items should be collected and the details needed for delivery.
Students can view errand requests that are currently open and available for acceptance.
A courier can accept an open errand request to become responsible for completing it.
Only one courier can be assigned to an errand request.
A requester cannot accept their own errand request.
A courier can mark an errand as picked up after collecting the requested items.
A courier can mark an errand as completed after delivering the items to the requester.
A requester can confirm that an errand has been delivered successfully.
A requester can cancel an errand request when cancellation is permitted.
An errand that is not accepted within the permitted duration can expire.
When an errand is canceled or expires, any credits reserved for that errand are released to the requester.
Each student receives an initial allocation of platform credits after registering.
The platform reserves the required credits from the requester when an errand is created.
Reserved credits are transferred to the courier after the errand is successfully completed.
Platform credits are used to compensate couriers for completing errands.
Platform credits cannot be purchased, withdrawn, or exchanged for money.
Payment for items collected from a supplier is handled outside the platform.
Suppliers are campus stores, facilities, or locations from which students can request errands.
The platform can provide a list of valid campus suppliers and pickup locations.
The platform does not need to provide supplier menus, product catalogs, inventory, or checkout.
The platform does not provide live location tracking for couriers while they are traveling.
Users must be able to register for an account and sign in before using account-based platform features.
Users can manage their profile information after registering.
The application should support complete errand workflows for both requesters and couriers on desktop and mobile screen sizes.
The application should provide feedback when an action is invalid or cannot be completed.
